The GPU-based Fast Hartley Transform (FHT) is a frequency-domain volume rendering method that replaces the Fourier transform with the Hartley transform to map real-valued input data directly to real-valued spectra [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the GPU-based Fast Hartley Transform (FHT) is a frequency-domain volume rendering method that replaces the Fourier transform with the Hartley transform to map real-valued input data directly to real-valued spectra. Source [S3] explicitly states that the Discrete Hartley Transform is used because it is a 'real transform if the input data is real' and avoids handling separate real and imaginary parts, effectively mapping real input to real output (N real numbers result in N real numbers, unlike the DFT which results in N complex numbers). Sources [S1] and [S2] confirm that FHT is used as an alternative to the Fourier transform in the context of GPU-based volume rendering (FVR) to reduce memory requirements, and describe the implementation details consistent with the claim.
